title: GAO Finds $1.3B in Missing F-35 Parts, the Pentagon Backs Neros With a $450M Drone Loan, and Turkey Launches the Mavi Balina-2026 Anti-Submarine Exercise
subhead: A US Government Accountability Office audit revealed that the Pentagon cannot account for more than 17,000 F-35 spare parts valued at $1.3 billion; the Defense Department extended a $450 million loan to Neros to scale domestic combat drone manufacturing; and the Turkish Navy opened the Mavi Balina-2026 anti-submarine warfare exercise in the Eastern Mediterranean with 8 submarines and 20 surface combatants.

sections.heading: F-35 Sustainment Audit, Base Force Protection, and NDAA Repair Dispute
sections.body:
An audit published by the Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that the Defense Department cannot verify the location or status of more than 17,000 F-35 Joint Strike Fighter spare parts valued at approximately $1.3 billion (Breaking Defense). Auditors attributed the discrepancy to disconnected property-tracking databases between prime contractor Lockheed Martin and Pentagon logistics commands. The findings come as aerospace trade associations intensify lobbying on Capitol Hill to remove service 'right to repair' mandates from the final text of the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (Breaking Defense).

To harden fifth-generation aircraft against low-cost aerial threats on the ground, the US Air Force is studying fixed and mobile anti-drone netting enclosures for F-35 hangars and flight lines at Tyndall Air Force Base in Florida (The War Zone). Simultaneously, US Air Forces in Europe raised security alert states at American bases in the United Kingdom—including RAF Mildenhall and RAF Lakenheath—following recent perimeter security assessments, while Air Force Global Strike Command began training B-1B Lancer bomber crews aboard contractor-operated HondaJet business aircraft to preserve bomber airframe hours (The War Zone).
sections.whyItMatters: Losing track of $1.3 billion in F-35 components weakens defense contractors' lobbying argument against congressional right-to-repair rules in the FY2027 NDAA.

sections.heading: Pentagon $450M Drone Financing, Forward Micro-Factories, and CCA Pricing
sections.body:
The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital finalized a $450 million loan guarantee for Neros Technologies to scale high-rate American manufacturing of first-person-view (FPV) combat drones and eliminate reliance on Asian sub-tier electronics (Defense News). Parallel fielding efforts are accelerating across the ground force: the US Army announced that 11 of its 12 active divisions have now received operational launched-effects drone kits, with the majority of airframes supplied by Griffon Aerospace (Breaking Defense).

To shorten resupply timelines in contested theaters, manufacturing startup Machina Labs secured a $9 million Pentagon contract to build LUCAS uncrewed aerial vehicles inside deployable, containerized robotic micro-factories near the front line (Defense News). On the higher end of autonomous airpower, Kratos Defense stated that unit costs for its combat-ready MQ-58 Valkyrie Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) now range between $6 million and $8 million depending on sensor payloads, while South Korea's Korean Air Aerospace announced plans to conduct initial flight tests of its indigenous CCA demonstrator before year-end (The War Zone, Breaking Defense).
sections.whyItMatters: Backing Neros with a $450 million loan while equipping 11 of 12 Army divisions with launched effects marks a shift from small experimental drone buys to industrial-scale US mass production.

sections.heading: Mavi Balina-2026 in the Eastern Mediterranean and Global Undersea Competition
sections.body:
The Turkish Naval Forces commenced the Mavi Balina-2026 (Blue Whale-2026) invitation exercise in the Eastern Mediterranean, bringing together 4,500 naval and air personnel, 8 submarines, 20 surface combatants, and 10 maritime patrol aircraft and helicopters through November 20 (Tolga Özbek). Alongside the exercise, Turkish software house HAVELSAN completed provisional acceptance testing for the Eastern Mediterranean Vessel Traffic Services (DAGTH) project, expanding coastal radar and maritime domain awareness across the Levant and Cyprus basins (Tolga Özbek).

Undersea competition also intensified in Northern Europe and East Asia. A consortium of British defense companies unveiled 'Arctic Hunter,' an uncrewed anti-submarine warfare platform converted from a 56-meter commercial fishing trawler capable of 60-day autonomous patrols across the GIUK gap, while Dutch sensor firm Optics11 entered negotiations to deploy seabed fiber-optic acoustic arrays capable of detecting surface tankers at ranges of 100 kilometers (The War Zone, Defense News). In East Asia, North Korean state media announced the test-firing of a new high-speed underwater torpedo system (CNA).
sections.whyItMatters: Concentrating eight submarines and 20 surface warships in the Eastern Mediterranean while activating HAVELSAN's coastal radar network gives Ankara continuous surface and subsurface surveillance across the Levant.

sections.heading: Hegseth Impeachment Filing, Naval War College Overhaul, and European Missiles
sections.body:
In Washington, Republican Representative Thomas Massie introduced an eight-article impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over unauthorized military operations in Iran, Yemen, and Venezuela (BBC, TRT Haber). Despite the congressional challenge, Hegseth traveled to Newport, Rhode Island, to issue 33 directives reforming the US Naval War College and broader professional military education—cutting civilian faculty positions and replacing traditional master's theses with AI-assisted classified wargaming (USNI News, Military Times). Separately, Pentagon space planners are studying a dedicated cislunar satellite constellation orbiting the Moon to track deep-space maneuvers (Ars Technica).

Across Europe and South Asia, Sweden's defense procurement agency (FMV) took delivery of German-built TAURUS KEPD 350 long-range cruise missiles scheduled for operational integration onto Swedish Air Force JAS 39 Gripen C/D fighters by 2028, while NATO tested 16 counter-drone systems from five vendors under a new 18-month rapid acquisition agreement (SavunmaSanayiST, M5 Dergi). In Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Russian forces launched 36 North Korean-made KN-23 ballistic missiles against Ukrainian power infrastructure in recent barrages, of which air defenses intercepted only four (M5 Dergi). Meanwhile, the Pakistan Air Force released an official operational video showcasing seven Turkish defense systems—including KAAN, AKINCI, Bayraktar TB2, KORKUT, and ŞAHİN—and Turkish firm SKYDAGGER revealed plans to dispense hundreds of mini kamikaze drones from Baykar's KIZILELMA unmanned fighter (SavunmaSanayiST).
sections.whyItMatters: Ukraine's interception of only four out of 36 North Korean KN-23 ballistic missiles shows that Pyongyang's missiles have become a primary strike tool against Ukrainian energy infrastructure as interceptor stocks tighten.

bottomLine: Pentagon logistics and industrial policy dominated Tuesday's defense agenda: a GAO audit uncovered $1.3 billion in untracked F-35 spare parts even as the Defense Department extended a $450 million loan to Neros for domestic combat drone manufacturing and the US Army confirmed launched-effects fielding across 11 of 12 divisions. In the Eastern Mediterranean, Turkey mobilized 8 submarines and 20 warships for the Mavi Balina-2026 anti-submarine exercise while HAVELSAN completed acceptance of its regional vessel traffic network. Elsewhere, Sweden received German TAURUS cruise missiles for its Gripen fleet, Pakistan showcased seven Turkish combat systems including KAAN and AKINCI, and Rep. Thomas Massie filed eight impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
sources: Breaking Defense, Defense News, The War Zone, USNI News, Military Times, Ars Technica, CNA, BBC, Tolga Özbek, SavunmaSanayiST, M5 Dergi, TRT Haber
